description: Step-based timeline showing matchstick triangle pattern growth from position 1 through 5. Each step adds a new position, shows the count, and updates the general expression 2n+1. Practice mode uses MCQ questions. Built with Singularity Design System.
topic: Matchstick Patterns and Setting Up Equations
contentReference: NCERT Ganita Prakash Grade 7 Part-II, Chapter 7 — Finding the Unknown
learningObjectives: Understand how triangle matchstick patterns grow with each position
Derive the general expression 2n+1 for the number of matchsticks at position n
Set up and solve linear equations based on pattern rules
Determine if a given number of matchsticks corresponds to a valid position

learn.title: The Triangle Pattern Begins
learn.description: At position 1, we build a single triangle using 3 matchsticks. This is the seed of our pattern!

learn.title: Growing the Pattern
learn.description: At position 2, we add another triangle sharing one side. Now we have 5 matchsticks total: 2×2 + 1 = 5.

learn.title: Position 3 — See the Rule?
learn.description: Adding one more triangle gives us 7 matchsticks: 2×3 + 1 = 7. Each new triangle adds exactly 2 sticks!

learn.title: Position 4 — The Pattern Holds
learn.description: At position 4, we have 9 matchsticks: 2×4 + 1 = 9. The formula 2n+1 works every time!

learn.title: Position 5 — General Rule: 2n + 1
learn.description: At position 5: 2×5 + 1 = 11 matchsticks. For any position n, the count is always 2n + 1.

practice.question: If 2n + 1 = 99, what is n?

practice.question: Is it possible to use exactly 200 matchsticks?

options.label: No, n is not a whole number

practice.explanation: 2n + 1 = 200 → n = 99.5. Not a whole number, so 200 sticks is impossible.

practice.description: Each new triangle increases the count by how many?
practice.question: How many new matchsticks does each added triangle need?
practice.explanation: Each new triangle shares one side, so only 2 new sticks are added.
